messages.subject: Re: can environment be passed to apps running via shiny-server?
messages.subject_clean: can environment be passed to apps running via shiny-server?
messages.body_plain:
Is there any way to stop shiny from scrubbing the environment variables?

We're using shiny server internally to try to host some applications. Unfortunately, the R process really needs the environment variables from the parent to work correctly (USER/LD_LIBRARY_PATH/etc). Just setting the environment variables in app.R doesn't seem to do the trick.

We can pass the correct variables to main.js, but when an R process is launched, it won't grab any of the required variables.

You'd have to have two different elements, one plotOutput and one plotlyOutput. In your ui.R:

  conditionalPanel("output.plot",
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  conditionalPanel("output.plotly",
    plotlyOutput("plotly")
  ),

In your server.R (assuming ua_vols_time_series is the non-plotly one):

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    switch(input$plot_type,
           ua_vols_time_series = ua_vols_time_series(input$dates[1],input$dates[2]),
           req(FALSE)
    )
  })
  output$plotly <- renderPlotly({

    switch(input$plot_type,
           ua_views_by_area = ua_views_by_area(input$dates[1],input$dates[2]),
           ua_age_access = ua_age_access(input$dates[1],input$dates[2]),

           req(FALSE)
    )
  })

The req(FALSE) call aborts the rendering of that output. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html.

messages.subject: Re: Resetting action buttons
messages.subject_clean: Resetting action buttons
messages.body_plain:
This line doesn't do what you think it does:

 observeEvent(input$goButton, {
     output$MyData <- renderDataTable({
   datasetInput()
   })
})

What I imagine you're thinking is, "When the goButton is clicked, update MyData to datasetInput()". But that's not what assignment to output$MyData means. It means, "This is the recipe for popuating MyData; update it as often as is necessary." So in sum, "When the goButton is clicked, update the recipe for populating MyData."

Replace that entire observeEvent with this:

output$MyData <- renderDataTable({
    req(input$goButton)
    isolate(datasetInput())
})

The line "req(input$goButton)" will do two things: 1) cause input$goButton to trigger the update of output$MyData, and 2) abort if the goButton has never been clicked before. And adding isolate() around datasetInput() will prevent changes in datasetInput from causing MyData to update.

messages.subject_clean: How can I use custom HTML attributes in Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm trying to build a custom HTML input widget in my Shiny app, and I need to be able to pass a single value in to the javascript functions that govern the input's functionality.

When I developed an initial prototype as a pure HTML page (see attached) I defined the value as a custom HTML attribute "data-n-available-traps" (with the data- attribute name following the required custom attribute naming convention).

I now want to be able to set up the HTML within Shiny using the tags() function, but if I set up the div like this:

            tags$div(id = "availableTrapsBox",
                data-n-available-traps = "4"
            )

but this fails because R interprets the hyphens in "data-n-available-traps" as minus signs.

Is there a way to use HTML data- custom attributes within Shiny, so that I can then use the div.dataset.nAvailableTraps in the JavaScript code to get the value?

Thanks very much,

Louise

messages.subject: Re: can environment be passed to apps running via shiny-server?
messages.subject_clean: can environment be passed to apps running via shiny-server?
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately not.

I've setup a shiny application that verbatimText displays:

- Sys.getenv("LD_LIBRARY_PATH")
- Sys.getenv("TEST_VARIABLE")
- Sys.getenv("USER")

And setup shiny server to run as a specific user through the configuration. Under that user's home directory, .bash_profile (which should be hit first) has an export statement that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH and TEST_VARIABLE. Running ./shiny-server and checking the application, it seems that TEST_VARIABLE and USER are blank, while LD_LIBRARY_PATH seems to be getting set in /R-3.2.2/lib64/R/etc/ldpaths.

Running the same application using runApp in a separate R Session has all these environment sessions set correctly.

Running R 3.2.2, Shiny Server 1.4, shiny 0.13.0.

Enter code here...

Ok, I figured out the problem.

Firstly, The conditionalPanels needed a condition. Sorry for not spotting that sooner, this is my first foray into Shiny (which is AWESOME!).

So I needed something like this in ui.R ...

 conditionalPanel("output.plot",
    condition = "input.plot_type == 'ploty_plot',
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  conditionalPanel("output.plotly",
    condition = "input.plot_type != 'ploty_plot',
    plotlyOutput("plotly")
  ),

Secondly, to get around the plot overlapping the UA areas, I put them on different rows ...

fluidRow(
   plotting panels here
),
hr()
fluidRow(
   UI here
)

Columns worked too, but the above looks nicer.

Thanks for the pointers Joe!

messages.subject: Re: Using Shiny to plot plotly and non-plotly plots in the same app
messages.subject_clean: Using Shiny to plot plotly and non-plotly plots in the same app
messages.body_plain:
Oh, it was my mistake. "output.plot" / "output.plotly" were supposed to be the conditions (so you can remove them if you want to use the conditions you came up with instead).

My mistake was that output.plot will never be true because output$plot isn't executing because the conditionalPanel is hidden because output.plot is false because the conditionalPanel is hidden... it's circular. This is because Shiny doesn't bother updating outputs that aren't visible. You can break this circular logic with outputOptions(output, "plot", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE) and outputOptions(output, "plotly", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE), then my "output.plot"/"output.plotly" should work.

But you could ignore that and just use your solution as well, maybe better your way anyway.

messages.subject: "Bouncing" range sliderInput when using controls to updateSliderInput
messages.subject_clean: "Bouncing" range sliderInput when using controls to updateSliderInput
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I'm working with a Shiny app, both developed and running in R 3.1.1 and shiny-server free version 1.1.0.10000, that has a number of range sliderInputs -- they're for setting an income range measured in % of the federal poverty level (just FYI) in a tabbed interface, so each tab gets its own uniquely-named FPL slider. eg, for the insurance ("ins") tab:

sliderInput("ins_income_group1",
   label="Use the Sliders to Select an Income Range (FPL%)",
   min= 0, max = 5,step=0.05, value=c(0,5), format="0%", ticks=FALSE)

These sliders have worked reliably, without the goofy behavior that inspired my question.

I added a pair of checkboxes to set a lower or upper bound, partly because it's not easy to land perfectly on 138% and partly because our step value of 5% is handy for other reasons:

#in ui.R
checkboxInput("ins_fpl138floor", "Set lower end of FPL range to 138%", FALSE),
checkboxInput("ins_fpl138ceil", "Set upper end of FPL range to 138%", FALSE)

# to keep server.R tidy, each tab's code is called via source(), eg source("tab_insurance.R", local=TRUE)
# here's how observe & updateSliderInput are coded in tab_insurance.R:
      observe({
        val_floor <- ifelse(input$ins_fpl138floor,1.38,input$ins_income_group1[1])
        val_ceil <- ifelse(input$ins_fpl138ceil,1.38,input$ins_income_group1[2])
        updateSliderInput(session, "ins_income_group1", value=c(val_floor,val_ceil))
      })

The checkboxes function as expected -- they set the upper (lower) value to 138% when ticked, "pull" back to 138% when ticked if the user selects a different value, and leaves the slider along when unticked. However, if you click and drag on one of the slider values, the slider will bounce between that value and some other value -- the "other" value isn't anything we've hardcoded or would otherwise expect to see -- a little faster than once per second. The other value on the range slider stays put.

We've reproduced this behavior on two different machines, in recent versions of Firefox and Chrome, and confirmed that we don't get this behavior when we remove the updateSliderInput code -- that is, the checkboxes alone aren't the issue. We've not had time, yet, to run locally, dig into logs, or do other sensible things -- we will, as time permits -- but perhaps the description of the symptoms and something about my code will reveal the answer to a more experienced/savvy Shiny programmer.

Cheers!
Colin Odden
Ohio State University

messages.subject: (non-)reactive matrix in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: (non-)reactive matrix in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am coding an app in which the user can define the number of columns in a matrix (note: the number of rows is hard-coded as a global variable, e.g. 2).
The user will then fill in this matrix one by one by pressing action buttons (i.e. after each button press, a number is filled into one coordinate of the matrix).

It sounds easy enough, but I can't seem to get it to work.

Here is a minimal code example of what I have so far:

(Note: you will need the shinyjs package to enable/disable widgets -> install.packages("shinyjs") & library(shinyjs) )

ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Enable functionalities of shinyjs package
  useShinyjs(),

  titlePanel("Test"),

  sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(

      # Choose number of columns in (reactive) matrix
      selectInput(inputId = "columns",
                  label = "Columns",
                  choices = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
                  selected = 1),

      # Fill in next coordinate in matrix
      actionButton(inputId = "press",
                   label = "Press"),

      # Continue with next row in matrix
      actionButton(inputId = "next_row",
                   label = "Next row"),

      # Reset app
      actionButton(inputId = "reset",
                   label = "Reset")

    ),

    mainPanel(

      plotOutput("plot")

    )

  )

))

server.R

## Global variable for number of rows in matrix
rows = 2

shinyServer(function(input, output){

  ## Reactive objects
  row <- reactiveValues(current = 1)
  col <- reactiveValues(current = 1)

  data <- reactive({matrix(NA, nrow = rows, ncol = as.integer(input$columns))})

  ## Toggle action buttons between active/nonactive when conditions
  ## are met or not respectively
  observe({toggleState("press", as.integer(input$columns) != 1
                                && col$current < as.integer(input$columns))})

  observe({toggleState("next_row", row$current != rows
                                   && col$current == as.integer(input$columns))})

  ## Execute code when buttons are pressed
  observeEvent(input$press, {

    disable("columns") # This disables the selectInput() widget to make sure you
                       # cannot change the number of columns while filling in
                       # the matrix

    col$current <- col$current + 1 # Increase column index by 1

    data_temp <- data() # Create temporary 'non-reactive' matrix
    data_temp[row$current, col$current] <- rnorm(1) # Fill in some value at the
                                                    # specified column
    print(data_temp)

  })

  observeEvent(input$next_row, {

    disable("columns")

    row$current <- row$current + 1 # Increase row index by 1
    col$current <- 1 # Reset column index to 1

    data_temp <- data()
    data_temp[row$current, col$current] <- rnorm(1)
    print(data_temp)

  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, {

    row$current <- 1 # reset row index
    col$current <- 1 # reset column index

    enable("columns")

  })

  # Return (empty) matrix to console whenever you change the number of columns.
  # Just to show the dimensions.
  output$plot <- renderPlot({

    print(data())

  })

})

Notes:
1) Everything is printed in the console, not in mainPanel()
2) The first coordinate of the matrix [1, 1] won't be filled in. You may ignore this.
3) When you choose 1 column, only the 'Next' button will be available. This is part of the bigger plan, so you may ignore this as well. Just choose 5 columns, and click on Press/Next to get the idea :)

I think the philosophy of the code should be:
1) Create reactive matrix

E.g. [,1] [,2]

[1,]  NA NA

[2,]  NA NA

2) Somehow transform reactive matrix to a 'non-reactive' matrix for storing data (i.e. similar to the reactiveValues() function) and fill it in

E.g. [,1] [,2]

[1,]    1    2

[2,]    3    4

3) Do analysis on the non-reactive matrix

E.g. sum of rows/columns

I already searched the internet for answers, but to no avail.

However, here are two discussions that helped me so far:
1) http://stackoverflow.com/questions/33651692/how-to-save-reactive-dataframe-as-non-reactive-in-shiny-r
(Anybody know how isolate() could fit in my case?)

2) https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/p2eElm-XaqQ/PmMX34CrCFMJ
and https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/p2eElm-XaqQ/5SRBJLedfh4J

Looking forward to hearing from the community! :)

Cheers

I'm working on an app that needs to load in a bigger shapefile to render in a leaflet map.

I've tried to add a progress bar to the renderLeaflet function like so:

output$map<-renderLeaflet({
     withProgress(message = 'Loading Map Data',
                  detail = 'Please be patient this may take a while...', value = 0, {
                    for (i in 1:60) {

   })

The problem is that the progress bar works finishes and then the map renders. So with the progress bar the map takes MUCH longer to render upwards of 20 seconds. messages.subject: Rounding Problem
messages.subject_clean: Rounding Problem
messages.body_plain:
I used cbind(round(xxx, 4), ...) inside renderTable(), but it only printed 2 significant digits.  Please help!
Specifically,

est_print = cbind(round(agr$Estimate$CCC,4),round(agr$Estimate$Precision,4),round(agr$Estimate$Accuracy,4), round(agr$Estimate$TDI,as.numeric(input$dec)), round(agr$Estimate$CP,4), round(agr$Estimate$RBS,2))
      conf_print = cbind(round(agr$Conf_Limit$CCC,4),round(agr$Conf_Limit$Precision,4),round(agr$Conf_Limit$Accuracy,4), round(agr$Conf_Limit$TDI,as.numeric(input$dec)), round(agr$Conf_Limit$CP,4), round(agr$Conf_Limit$RBS,2))
      allo_print = cbind(round(agr$Allowance$CCC,4),round(agr$Allowance$Precision,4),round(agr$Allowance$Accuracy,4), round(agr$Allowance$TDI,as.numeric(input$dec)), round(agr$Allowance$CP,4), round(agr$Allowance$RBS,2))
      mytable <- rbind(est_print,conf_print,allo_print)
      colnames(mytable) <- c("CCC","Precision","Accuracy","TDI","CP","RBS")
      rownames(mytable) <- c("Statistic","95% CL","Allowance")
      myxtable <- xtable(mytable)
      myxtable

and I got
CCC  Precision  Accuracy  TDI  CP  RBS
Statistic  0.99  0.99  1.00  127.49  0.95  0.00
95% CL  0.98  0.98  1.00  136.39  0.93
Allowance  0.98  150.00  0.90

Hi,

I have a question, sorry if it be something obvious.

I am doing a app for a class and I need to download the output (tables, images, etc). I am using a downloadHandler() like the runExample("10_download"), but I can´t save the output in a specific location in my computer. I choose my workspace or a specific folder to save a .txt, but nothing is saving there. The same situations happen with the exemple 10, I can´t save the data "rock" or "car" in this especific space.

How I choose the spacific space to save my output (.txt) using downloadHandler()?

Thanks
Filipe
